curriculum.lesson_evidence: Striking and bouncing are fundamental movement skills. To strike a ball or balloon, stand side-on, keep your eyes on the object, swing level and follow through. To bounce a ball, use your fingertips (not a flat palm), push the ball down to about waist height, keep it slightly to the side of your body and lift your head so you can see what is around you. More force does not give more control; steady timing does.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Chloe bounces the ball with a flat, stiff hand and the ball bounces too high and rolls away. Write two cues that would help and say why.

FEEDBACK
Cues: 'use your fingertips, not your palm' and 'push the ball down to waist height'. Fingertips give control and a lower, steady bounce, so the ball stays close.

WATCH FOR
Thinking that hitting or bouncing harder gives more control. More force sends the ball farther away; control comes from technique and timing.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Using a bouncing ball and a soft object to strike (a balloon works well indoors), practise 20 bounces with each hand and 10 gentle strikes. Record your best streak for each, choose one cue and retest. Use a clear space away from breakable things.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.
